Plain language summary


We found 51 studies including randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and observational
studies with a mixed risk of bias. Respiratory virus spread might be prevented by
hygienic measures around younger children. These might also reduce transmission
from children to other household members. Implementing barriers to transmission,
isolation, and hygienic measures may be effective at containing respiratory virus
epidemics. There was limited evidence that (more uncomfortable and expensive)
N95 masks were superior to simple ones. Adding virucidals or antiseptics to normal
handwashing is of uncertain benefit. There is insufficient evaluation of global
measures such as screening at entry ports and social distancing.
